The defendant did not make payment of the outstanding amount.

It is stated that in discharge of its part liability, defendant had issued two cheques, i.e cheque bearing Nos.003255, dated 14.04.2022, for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- and cheque bearing No.003256, dated 16.04.2022, for a sum of Rs.1,15,750/-, both drawn on ICICI Bank, Sector-3, Rohini Branch, both of which got dishonoured/bounced on presentation thereof by the plaintiff to its bank.
The plaintiff accordingly sent legal notice on 16.09.2024, the tracking report whereof suggests that the same was duly served upon the defendant.

3. Therefore, the plaintiff has filed the instant suit against the defendant, inter alia seeking a decree in the sum of Rs.4,62,880/- (Rupees Four Lakhs Sixty Two Thousand Eight Hundred Eighty Only)

4. It is pertinent to mention here that prior to filing the present suit, plaintiff had also exhausted the remedy of pre-institution mediation in terms of Section 12-A of Commercial Courts Act, 2015.
Despite service of pre-institution mediation notice, the defendant did not give his consent and willingness to participate in the mediation process.
Accordingly, Certificate of Non-Starter Report dated 22.11.2024 was issued in the matter.

. After getting served with the summons, defendant filed written statement, inter alia admitting the receipt of goods, however, putting serious questions marks on the quality thereof by stating that the goods supplied by the plaintiff were duplicate/fake/sub-standard/inferior quality.

The defendant has questioned the entitlement of plaintiff to recover the suit amount from it on the basis of aforesaid FIR.
6. Plaintiff filed replication, inter alia denying the averments made in the written statement and reiterating the ones made in the plaint.
7. With these pleadings of the parties, vide order dated 09.07.2025, following issues were settled for trial in the matter:
